Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 1:

Surat al-Kahf [Meccan, except for "and restrain yourself" (wa-isbir nafsak) verse; it has one hundred and ten verses, or fifteen verses]. It was revealed after Surat al-Ghashiyah.

﴿Praise﴾ (al-hamd), which is the attribution of beauty, is established ﴿for Allah﴾ the Exalted. Is the intended meaning to inform [people] of this so that they believe in it, or to glorify Him with it, or both? These are possibilities, the most beneficial of which is the third.

﴿Who sent down upon His servant﴾ Muhammad ﴿the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿and did not make in it﴾ i.e., in it, ﴿any crookedness﴾, meaning discrepancy or contradiction. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring back to "the Book".

[Qayyiman] mustaqiman (upright, straight), a second circumstantial qualifier (hal thaniya) serving as emphasis. [Li-yundhira] yukhawwif bil-kitab (he warns with the Book) al-kafirin (the disbelievers) [ba'san] adhaban (a punishment) [shadidan min ladunhu] min qibal Allah (from the side of God).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 3:

﴿Abiding therein forever﴾ — it is Paradise.

[Ḥ] And to warn (wa-yundhir) those among the disbelievers...

Note on the passage: the Jalalayn gloss here is a short fragment, so the translation above reflects the text as given. The verse's wording is: ﴿And warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 5:

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, of this statement, ﴿nor did their fathers﴾, who came before them and who said it. ﴿How monstrous is the word that comes out of their mouths!﴾ How great it is, in magnitude. The word (kalima) is a specification (tamyiz) explaining the vague pronoun, and the thing being condemned is omitted, meaning: their statement mentioned above. ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾: in that matter, ﴿but a lie﴾ (maqulan), that is, a statement uttered.

Perhaps you would destroy (ﷺ) yourself... Let me correct that rendering to keep the text faithful:

﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief﴾ (*bākhiʿ*, meaning "destroying" or "killing") ﴿over their traces﴾ after them, that is, after their turning away from you, ﴿if they do not believe in this discourse﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿in sorrow﴾ out of anger and grief from you because of your eagerness for their faith. Its case ending (*naṣbuh*) is accusative as a *maf'ūl lahu* (object of purpose, or cause, in Arabic grammar).

We have made what is on the earth—of animals, plants, trees, rivers, and other things—an adornment for it, so that We may test them: to try people, as they look upon it, as to which of them is best in deed, that is, most detached from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 8:

﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust﴾, crumbled fragments, ﴿dry﴾, withered, not producing growth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 9:

﴿Did you think﴾ i.e., did you suppose ﴿that the People of the Cave﴾ the cave in the mountain ﴿and the Raqim﴾ the inscribed tablet on which their names and lineages were written. The Prophet (ﷺ) had been asked about their story. ﴿They were﴾ in their story ﴿among﴾ the category of ﴿Our signs, a marvel﴾. The predicate of "kana" (was) and what precedes it is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: they were a marvel beyond the rest of the signs, or the most marvelous of them. The matter is not so.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 10:

﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾ (ʿaṭāʾ, plural of fatan, which is a complete, mature young man), fearing for their faith from their people, the disbelievers. ﴿So they said: "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself"﴾ (min ladunka: from Your side). ﴿And facilitate for us our affair with right guidance﴾ (wa-hayyiʾ: set right, make ready) ﴿rashadan﴾ (meaning: guidance).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 11:

﴿So We struck upon their ears﴾ i.e., We made them sleep, ﴿in the cave for a number of years﴾ counted, numbered.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 12:

﴿Then We roused them﴾ (ba'athnahum), i.e., We woke them up. ﴿That We might know﴾ (linan'lam), with the knowledge of witnessing (ʿilm mushāhadah), ﴿which of the two parties﴾ (ayyu al-hizbayn), the two groups that differed concerning the length of their stay, ﴿was most accurate﴾ (aḥṣā), an elative form meaning more precise (bi-ma'na adbaṭ), ﴿in computing﴾ (limā labithū), i.e., for their stay; the phrase (limā labithū) is connected to what follows it, ﴿the term﴾ (amadan), i.e., the duration.
﴿Naḥnu naqussu﴾ (We relate) we recite, ﴿ʿalayka nabaʾahum bil-ḥaqq﴾ to you their account in truth, i.e., with sincerity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 14:

﴿And We fortified their hearts﴾ We strengthened them to speak the truth ﴿when they stood up﴾ before their king, who had commanded them to prostrate to the idols, ﴿and said: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we shall never call upon any god besides Him"﴾ i.e., other than Him ﴿—for then we would have uttered an outrageous thing (shatat)﴾ i.e., a saying of shatat, meaning excess (ifrat) in disbelief, if we were to call upon a god other than Allah, hypothetically.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 15:

﴿These﴾: مُبْتَدَأ (mubtada', the subject of a nominal sentence). ﴿Our people﴾: عَطْف بَيان ('atf bayan, explicative apposition). ﴿Have taken besides Him gods.﴾ ﴿Why not﴾ هَلّا (would that... / why do they not) ﴿bring upon them﴾ [proof] ﴿concerning their worship﴾ ﴿with clear authority﴾ with an evident proof. ﴿Who is more unjust﴾ i.e., no one is more unjust ﴿than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾ by attributing a partner to Him, exalted is He. Some of the youths said to one another:

﴿And when you withdraw from them and from what they worship other than Allah, then take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you a means of ease in your affair﴾ (مِرْفَقًا). It is read with a kasra (the short vowel "i") on the mim and a fatha (the short vowel "a") on the fa', and vice versa (مَرْفِقًا), meaning what you draw benefit from of food for lunch and dinner.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 17:

﴿And you would see the sun, when it rose, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it set, passing them on the left, while they were in a spacious place within it.﴾ (تزاور, read with tashdid or takhfif) means it inclines, ﴿away from their cave to the right﴾ meaning away from its side, ﴿and when it set, passing them on the left﴾ meaning it leaves them and passes by them, so that it does not touch them at all, ﴿while they were in a spacious place within it﴾ meaning a roomy part of the cave where the cold breeze and its gentle air reach them. ﴿That﴾ mentioned ﴿is among the signs of Allah﴾ meaning proofs of His power.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 18:

﴿And you would think them awake﴾ if you saw them, ﴿awake﴾, i.e., alert, because their eyes were open, the plural of "yaqiz" with a kasra on the qaf, ﴿while they were asleep﴾, the plural of "raqid", meaning sleeping. ﴿And We turned them to the right and to the left﴾ so that the earth would not consume their flesh. ﴿And their dog stretched forth its forelegs﴾, i.e., its two hands, ﴿at the threshold﴾, at the courtyard of the cave. Whenever they turned over, it would turn over with them, like them in sleeping and waking. ﴿Had you looked upon them, you would have turned from them in flight, and you would have been filled﴾ (read with both tashdid and takhfif) ﴿with dread of them﴾ (the ayn read with sukun and with damma), for Allah had restrained anyone from entering upon them by means of dread.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 19:

﴿And thus﴾ as We did to them what We have mentioned, ﴿We raised them up﴾ We awakened them ﴿that they might question one another﴾ about their state and the duration of their stay. ﴿A speaker among them said: "How long have you remained?" They said: "We have remained a day or part of a day."﴾ Because they had entered the cave at sunrise and were raised at sunset, they thought it was the sunset of the day they had entered. ﴿Then they said﴾ hesitantly regarding this, ﴿"Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours﴾ (with the letter rā' pronounced with sukūn or with kasra), ﴿to the city﴾ said to be the one now called Tarsus (with the rā' pronounced with fatha), ﴿and let him see which of them has the purest food﴾ i.e., which of the city's foods is most lawful.
Indeed, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you ﴿to death by stoning﴾ or force you back into their creed. And you will never prosper then ﴿i.e., if you return to their creed﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 18, verse 21:

﴿And thus﴾ as We raised them up, ﴿We made it known﴾ (a'thara), meaning We informed ﴿about them﴾ their people and the believers, ﴿that they might know﴾, i.e. their people, ﴿that the promise of Allah﴾ regarding the Resurrection ﴿is true﴾, by way of this reasoning: the One who is able to put them to sleep for a long period and keep them alive in their state without food is able to bring the dead back to life. ﴿And that the Hour, there is no doubt﴾, no uncertainty ﴿concerning it﴾. ﴿When﴾ (idh) is a ma'mul (an element governed) of a'thharna. ﴿They disputed﴾, i.e. the believers and the disbelievers, ﴿among themselves concerning their affair﴾, the affair of the youths, regarding the construction around them. ﴿So they said﴾, i.e. the disbelievers, ﴿Build over them﴾, i.e. around them, ﴿a structure﴾ that will cover them. ﴿Their Lord knows best about them.﴾ ﴿Those who prevailed over their affair﴾, the affair of the youths, and they were the believers, ﴿said: We will surely take over them﴾, i.e. around them, ﴿a place of worship﴾ in which prayer is performed. This was done at the entrance of the cave.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 22:

﴿They will say﴾ i.e., those who disputed about the number of the young men (ahl al-kahf) at the time of the Prophet ﷺ, i.e., some of them will say: ﴿They were three, the fourth of them being their dog﴾, and [others] ﴿will say: five, the sixth of them being their dog﴾ — both statements belong to the Christians of Najran — ﴿guessing at the unseen﴾, i.e., conjecture about what is hidden from them. It refers to both statements together, and it is in the accusative as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), i.e., because of their supposition. ﴿And they will say﴾, i.e., the believers: ﴿Seven, and the eighth of them is their dog﴾. The sentence consisting of the subject and its predicate is a description of "seven," with the waw added; it has been said that it is for emphasis, or to indicate the attachment of the description to the described. The description of the first two with "guessing" but not the third is evidence that the third is the accepted and correct one. ﴿Say: My Lord knows best their number; none knows them except a few.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am among the few," and he counted them as seven. ﴿So do not argue﴾, i.e., do not dispute ﴿concerning them except with an outward argument﴾, based on what has been revealed to you. ﴿And do not seek a ruling concerning them﴾, i.e., do not ask for a legal opinion (futya) ﴿from any of them﴾, i.e., from the People of the Book, the Jews, ﴿anyone﴾. The people of Mecca asked him about the story of the people of the Cave, and he said: "I will inform you of it tomorrow," and did not say "if Allah wills," so [this verse] was revealed.
﴿And never say of anything﴾, that is, concerning something, ﴿"Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,"﴾, that is, in the time to come.

﴿unless Allah wills﴾, meaning: unless you are connected to the will of Allah, the Exalted, by saying, "if Allah wills." ﴿And remember your Lord﴾, meaning: His will, attaching yourself to it, ﴿when you forget﴾. Its remembrance after forgetting is like its remembrance together with the utterance. Al-Hasan and others said: it applies as long as one remains in the session. ﴿And say: "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this"﴾, meaning: from the account of the People of the Cave, as a proof of my prophethood. ﴿to right guidance﴾, meaning: guidance. And Allah did that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 25:

﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred﴾ with tanwin (nunation, the final "-n" sound on ﴿مائة﴾), ﴿years﴾. ﴿Sinin﴾ (years) is in apposition (ʿatf bayan, explanatory apposition) to ﴿thalatha mi'a﴾ (three hundred). These three hundred years, according to the People of the Cave, are solar years (shamsiyya, solar reckoning), and the lunar (qamariyya) years exceed them by nine years according to the Arabs. I have already mentioned this in His words ﴿and they added nine﴾, meaning nine years. So the three hundred solar years are three hundred and nine lunar years.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 26:

﴿Say, "Allah knows best how long they remained."﴾ Among those who differed about it, and this is what was mentioned earlier. ﴿To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, His knowledge [belongs]. ﴿How clearly He sees, and how clearly He hears!﴾ That is, by Allah; it is a form of exclamation (ta'ajjub). Likewise, ﴿how clearly He hears﴾ is in the sense of "how much He sees" and "how much He hears." These two are used figuratively, and the intended meaning is that nothing is hidden from His sight and His hearing. ﴿They have no protector besides Him﴾ for the people of the heavens and the earth, ﴿no ally (waliyy)﴾ meaning helper. ﴿And He does not make anyone share in His command﴾ because He is free of need of a partner.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 27:

﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. None can alter His words, and you will never find any refuge other than Him.﴾ *malja’* (refuge)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 28:

﴿And restrain yourself﴾ hold yourself back ﴿along with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face﴾ by their worship, ﴿seeking His Face﴾ the Exalted, not anything of the worldly goods, and they are the poor ﴿and let not your eyes pass beyond them﴾ turn away from them; he expressed by the two eyes the one who possesses them ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life. And do not obey him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾ i.e., the Qur'an; he is ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and his companions ﴿and who follows his desire﴾ in polytheism ﴿and whose affair is excess﴾ extravagance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 29:

﴿And say﴾ to him and to his companions: this Qur'an is ﴿the truth from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve﴾. It is a threat to them. ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿a Fire whose enclosure surrounds them﴾, meaning its enclosure encompasses them. ﴿And if they ask for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal﴾, like the dregs of olive oil, ﴿which scalds the faces﴾, because of its heat when brought near to them. ﴿How wretched the drink!﴾, that is, it. ﴿And how evil a resting-place﴾, i.e., the Fire. Murtafaqan (resting-place) is a tamyiz (specification) transferred from the subject, meaning: how ugly is its resting-place. It stands in contrast to His statement later about Paradise: ﴿and how good a resting-place﴾. Otherwise, what resting-place is there in the Fire?

Verse 30 of Surah al-Kahf, "Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—indeed, We do not allow the reward of anyone who does good deeds to be lost," is the predicate (khabar) of "inna" in "Indeed, those who..." Within it is the placing of the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun (iqamat al-zahir maqam al-mudmar), and the meaning is "their reward," i.e., We reward them for what it contains.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 31:

﴿For them are Gardens of Eden﴾ (a dwelling), ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾; ﴿they will be adorned therein with bracelets﴾ of gold. It has been said that "min" (from) here is extra (ziyada), and it has been said that it is partitive (lil-tab'id); and the word is the plural of aswira, like ahmira, the plural of siwar (bracelet). ﴿of gold. And they will wear green garments of sundus﴾, which is what is thin of brocade (dibaj), ﴿and istabraq﴾, which is what is thick of it. And in the verse of ar-Rahman: ﴿its linings of istabraq﴾. ﴿Reclining therein on couches﴾, the plural of arika, which is the bed (sarir) inside the hajala, a chamber adorned with garments and curtains for the bride. ﴿How excellent a reward﴾, that is, the recompense, the Garden.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 32:

﴿Wa-drib﴾ (And set forth) ij'al (make) ﴿lahum﴾ (for them), i.e., for the disbelievers together with the believers, ﴿mathalan rajulayn﴾ (an example: two men). "Rajulayn" is a substitute (badal), and it and what follows it are an explanation of "mathal" (the example). ﴿Ja'alna li-ahadihima﴾ (We made for one of them), namely the disbeliever, ﴿jannatayn﴾ (two gardens), i.e., two orchards ﴿min a'nab﴾ (of grapevines), ﴿wa-hafafnahuma bi-nakhl﴾ (and We surrounded them with palm trees), ﴿wa-ja'alna baynahuma zar'an﴾ (and We placed between them cultivated land) ﴿yaqtatu bihi﴾ (from which one derives sustenance).

﴿Both of the gardens﴾: "kilta" (كِلْتا) is singular in form but denotes the dual. It is the mubtada' (grammatical subject of a nominal sentence). ﴿brought forth its produce﴾ ("ātat," آتَتْ) is its khabar (predicate). "Ukulahā" (أُكُلها) means its fruit (thamaruhā). ﴿and did not fall short﴾ ("wa lam tazlim," وَلَمْ تَظْلِم) means it did not diminish (tanqus). ﴿And We caused to gush forth﴾ ("wa fajjarnā," وَفَجَّرْنا), that is, We split (open the earth) (shaqaqnā). ﴿between them a river﴾ ("khilālahumā nahran," خِلالهما نَهَرًا) flowing between them (yajrī baynahumā).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 34:

﴿And he had fruit﴾ in addition to the two gardens. [It is read] with a fatha on the tha' and the mim, and with a damma on both, and with a damma on the first and a sukun on the second. It is the plural of thamara (fruit), like shajara (tree) and shajar, khashaba (piece of wood) and khashab, and badana (camel for sacrifice) and badan. ﴿So he said to his companion﴾, the believer, ﴿while he was disputing with him﴾, boasting to him, ﴿"I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men"﴾, i.e., in kinsmen (ʿashīra).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 35:

﴿And he entered his garden⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ with his companion, taking him around within it and showing him its fruits.⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ He did not say "his two gardens" because he intended the orchard (rawda) as a whole. It was also said that he used the singular for brevity, since one suffices.⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ And he was a wrongdoer to himself⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ through disbelief⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿, he said: "I do not think that this will ever perish⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿,"⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿ meaning, that it will be annihilated.⁠

And I do not think the Hour will be established; and even if I am returned to my Lord (in the Hereafter, as you claim), I will surely find better than it as a destination (munqalaban), a place of return.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 37:

﴿He said to him his companion, while he was disputing with him﴾ replying to him ﴿Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust﴾ because Adam was created from it ﴿then from a drop [of semen]﴾, i.e., of seminal fluid (maniyy) ﴿then fashioned you﴾ made you proportionate and shaped you.

﴿But I﴾. Its original form is لَكِنْ أنا (lākin anā). Either the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the nūn, or the hamza was dropped and then the nūn was assimilated into a following nūn (idghām, assimilation of one consonant into another). ﴿He﴾ is a ḍamīr al-sha'n (a pronoun referring to the matter or situation, rather than to a specific person), and the clause that follows it explains it. The meaning is: "I say."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 39:

﴿Wa-lawlā﴾ (why not), ﴿idh dakhalta jannataka qulta﴾ (when you entered your garden, you should have said) upon being amazed by it, ﴿mā shā’a Allāh, lā quwwata illā billāh﴾ ("Whatever Allah wills [will be]; there is no power except through Allah").

And in the hadith: "Whoever is given something good from his family or wealth and says at that moment, 'Whatever Allah wills [will be]; there is no power except through Allah,' will see nothing disliked in it." 

﴿in tarani anā﴾ (if you see me as less than you in wealth and children): the word ﴿anā﴾ (I) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) between the two objects.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 18, verse 40:

﴿Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ is the answer to the condition (jawab al-shart). ﴿And He will send upon it a calamity (husban)﴾ — its plural is husbanah, meaning thunderbolts (sawa'iq) ﴿from the sky, so that it becomes a barren, slippery ground (sa'idan zalaqan)﴾ — a smooth land on which no foot can stand firm.

﴿Or its water becomes sunken﴾ (*ghawran*, غَوْرًا), meaning *ghā'iran* (غائِرًا, sinking away), coordinated (*'atf*, عَطْف, grammatical coordination) with *yursil* (يُرْسِل, "sends") rather than with *tuṣbiḥ* (تُصْبِح, "becomes"), because the sinking of water is not caused by thunderbolts. ﴿So you will not be able to find for it a seeking﴾: no stratagem (*ḥīla*, حِيلَة) by which you could reach it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 18, verse 42:

﴿And his fruit was encompassed (by ruin)﴾ by the aforementioned means of destruction, along with his garden, by ruin, so it was destroyed. ﴿So he began to turn over his palms﴾ in regret and remorse ﴿over what he had spent on it﴾, on the cultivation of his garden, ﴿while it lay﴾ fallen ﴿upon its trellises﴾, its supports for the vines, meaning the trellises fell, then the vines fell upon them. ﴿And he says, "Would that"﴾ (the "yā" here is li-l-tanbīh, for alerting) ﴿I...﴾

﴿And he had no﴾ company, read with the *ta'* (تَكُنْ) and the *ya'* (يَكُنْ), ﴿of helpers who would aid him against God﴾, ﴿when it was destroyed﴾, ﴿nor could he defend himself﴾ ﴿when it was destroyed by himself﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 44:

﴿There, at that time﴾ i.e., the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the guardianship﴾ — with a fatha on the waw, it means victory/support (al-nusrah), and with a kasra it means dominion (al-mulk) — ﴿belongs to Allah, the True﴾ — with raf‘ (damma) it is an adjective of al-wilayah, and with jarr (kasra) it is an adjective of the Name of Majesty (al-jalalah) — ﴿He is best in reward﴾ than the reward of other than Him, if the other were to reward, ﴿and best in outcome﴾ — with a damma or sukun on the qaf, meaning the final result for the believers — and the nasb of both is as a tamyiz (specification).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 45:

﴿And strike for them﴾ make (ṣayyir) for them, i.e., for your people, ﴿the example of the life of this world﴾ — the first object (maf'ūl awwal) — ﴿like water﴾ — the second object (maf'ūl thānin) — ﴿which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it﴾ it became dense (takāthafa) because of the descent of the water, ﴿the vegetation of the earth﴾. Or, the water mingled with the plants, so they were watered and became beautiful. ﴿Then it becomes﴾ became, ﴿dry stalks﴾ dried up, its parts scattered (muta­farriqa), ﴿which the winds scatter﴾ disperse and spread out, ﴿so they carry it away﴾. The meaning: He likened the worldly life to a beautiful plant that dried up and broke, and the winds scattered it. In another reading, "al-riyāḥ" (the winds) is read as "al-rīḥ" (the wind). ﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Omnipotent﴾ capable (qādiran).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 46:

﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world﴾ by which one beautifies oneself in it. ﴿But the enduring good deeds﴾ are "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to God), "al-hamdu lillah" (praise be to God), "la ilaha illa Allah" (there is no god but God), and "Allahu akbar" (God is greatest). Some have added, "la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah" (there is no power and no strength except with God). ﴿are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for hope﴾, i.e., what a person hopes for and expects from God, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 47:

﴿On the Day We set the mountains in motion﴾ they will be removed from the surface of the earth, and so they will become scattered dust particles (habaʾ munbathth). In another reading, it is recited with the nūn and with a kasra on the yāʾ and a fatḥa on al-jibāl (i.e., nusayyir is read as nusayyiru, with the mountains as the object). ﴿And you will see the earth laid bare﴾ manifest, with nothing upon it of mountain or anything else. ﴿And We will gather them﴾ the believers and the disbelievers ﴿and leave out none﴾ we will not leave behind.

[Qur'an 18:48] "And they will be presented before your Lord in rows" — a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning arranged in lines, each nation in a row. And it will be said to them: "You have come to Us just as We created you the first time," — meaning individually, barefoot, naked, uncircumcised (ghurlan). And it is said to those who denied resurrection: "Rather, you claimed that We would never appoint for you an appointment" — here "an" (أنْ) is a lightened form (mukhaffafa) of the heavy one (thaqīla), meaning that He (annahu) would never appoint for you a fixed time (mawʿidan) for the resurrection (al-baʿth).

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, the book of each person, in the right hand of the believers and in the left hand of the disbelievers. ﴿And you will see the criminals﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿fearful of what is in it. And they will say﴾ upon seeing what it contains of misdeeds: ﴿Woe to us!﴾ ("Yā" is for alerting; "waylatanā" means ruin, destruction, and it is a verbal noun with no verb of its own from its root), ﴿what is this Book that leaves nothing small or great﴾ of our sins ﴿except that it has enumerated it﴾, counted it and recorded it. They marvel at it in this respect, ﴿and they will find what they did present﴾, recorded in their book. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾, meaning He does not punish him without sin, nor does He diminish the reward of a believer.

﴿وإذْ﴾ (and when) is in the accusative case, governed by ﴿اذْكُرْ﴾ (remember).

﴿قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ اُسْجُدُوا لِآدَم﴾ (We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"). The prostration meant is one of bowing (sujud inhina'), not placing the forehead on the ground. It was a greeting of honour (tahiyya) to him.

﴿فَسَجَدُوا إلّا إبْلِيس كانَ مِن الجِنّ﴾ (so they prostrated, except Iblis; he was of the jinn). It has been said that they (the jinn) were a kind of angel, so the exception (istithna', exception) is connected (muttasil). It has also been said that it is disconnected (munqati', separate), and that Iblis is the father of the jinn, so he has offspring, who are mentioned after him, whereas the angels have no offspring.

﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أمْر رَبّه﴾ (so he defied the command of his Lord), i.e., he went outside His obedience by abandoning prostration.

﴿أفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُ وذُرِّيَّته﴾ (Will you then take him and his offspring) — the address is to Adam and his offspring, and the pronoun in both places refers to Iblis.

﴿أوْلِياء مِن دُونِي﴾ (as protectors instead of Me), i.e., you obey them.

﴿وهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوّ﴾ (while they are an enemy to you) — ﴿عَدُوّ﴾ here means enemies, and the clause is a circumstantial phrase (hal).

﴿بِئْسَ لِلظّالِمِينَ بَدَلًا﴾ (evil is the exchange for the wrongdoers). Iblis and his offspring, in being obeyed, are the substitute (badal) for obeying God.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 18, verse 51:

﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾, i.e., Iblis and his offspring; ﴿I did not cause some of them to witness the creation of others﴾. ﴿Nor would I have taken the misleaders﴾, the devils, ﴿as helpers﴾ (ʿaḍud), i.e., assistants, ﴿in creation﴾. So how can you obey them?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 52:

﴿And [mention] the Day﴾ is in the accusative, governed by [the verb] "remember" (udhkur). ﴿He will say﴾ — read with the ya' and the nun. ﴿"Call upon My partners,"﴾ meaning the idols, ﴿"whom you claimed"﴾ would intercede for you according to your assumption. ﴿So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾ — they will not answer them. ﴿And We will place between them﴾ — between the idols and those who worshipped them ﴿a barrier (mawbiqan)﴾ — a valley from the valleys of Hell in which they will all perish. It is derived from waqaba, with a fatha, meaning "he perished."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 18, verse 53:

﴿And the criminals will see the Fire, and they will realize﴾ i.e., they will be certain, ﴿that they are going to fall into it﴾ i.e., that they will be cast into it, ﴿and will find no escape from it﴾ i.e., no place to turn away to.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 54:

﴿And We have certainly diversified﴾ We made clear ﴿in this Qur'an for the people every kind of example﴾, an adjective of an omitted noun, meaning: an example of the same kind as every example, so that they may take heed. ﴿And man is ever⁠ the most contentious of things﴾, i.e., the disbeliever, ﴿in disputation﴾, in contention regarding falsehood. ﴿Most contentious﴾ is a tamyiz (specification) transferred from the subject of kana (was), and the meaning is: the disputation of man was the most contentious thing in him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 55:

﴿And what prevented the people﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿from believing﴾ (the second object of the verb), ﴿when the guidance﴾ (the Qur'an) ﴿had come to them, and from asking their Lord for forgiveness, except that the way of the former peoples should come upon them﴾ (the subject of the verb), i.e., Our custom concerning them, which is the destruction decreed for them, ﴿or that the punishment should come upon them face to face﴾ (qubulan: meaning confrontation and direct sight), and this is killing on the day of Badr. In another reading, it is read with two dammas, as the plural of qabil, i.e., kinds (of punishment).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 56:

﴿And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good news﴾ to the believers ﴿and warners﴾ frightening the disbelievers. ﴿But those who disbelieve dispute by means of falsehood﴾ by their saying: ﴿Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?﴾ and the like, ﴿in order to refute thereby﴾ i.e., to invalidate through their disputation ﴿the truth﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿and they take My signs﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and that with which they were warned﴾ of the Fire ﴿in mockery﴾ (huzuw), i.e., ridicule.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 57:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forward?﴾ That is, what he has done of disbelief and sins. ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾, that is, veils, ﴿lest they understand it﴾, i.e., from understanding the Qur'an, meaning they do not understand it; ﴿and in their ears is deafness﴾, a heaviness, so that they do not hear it. ﴿And if you invite them to guidance, they will never be guided, then﴾, i.e., by the arrangement mentioned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 58:

﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, Possessor of mercy. If He were to take them to task for what they have earned, He would hasten for them the punishment﴾ in this world ﴿but for them is an appointed time﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and they will not find other than Him a refuge﴾, a place of refuge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 59:

﴿And those towns﴾, i.e., their people, like ʿĀd and Thamūd and others, ﴿We destroyed them when they did wrong﴾, i.e., disbelieved, ﴿and We appointed for their destruction﴾, i.e., for their annihilation; and in another reading, with a fatḥah on the mīm, i.e., for their *halāk* (ruin).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 60:

﴿When Musa said﴾ he is the son of Imran, ﴿to his young man﴾ Yusha' ibn Nun, who used to follow him, serve him, and take knowledge from him. ﴿I will not cease﴾ I will not stop travelling ﴿until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾ the junction of the Sea of Rum (the Mediterranean) and the Sea of Persia (the Persian Gulf), on the side toward the east; i.e., the place that gathers that, ﴿or I will journey for ages﴾ a long period of time in reaching it, if it is far away.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 61:

﴿So when they reached the meeting-place of the two seas﴾ between the two seas, ﴿they forgot their fish﴾. Yusha' forgot to carry it when they set off, and Musa forgot to remind him. ﴿And it took its way into the sea﴾ i.e., it made its way by Allah's making. ﴿Saraban﴾ i.e., like a tunnel (sarab), which is a long cleft with no passage through it. This was because Allah held back the flow of the water from the fish, so the water parted from it and it remained like a window that had not closed, and what was beneath it of it froze.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 62:

﴿Then when they had passed beyond it﴾ that place, by travelling until the time of the morning meal on the second day, ﴿he said﴾ Musa, ﴿to his servant: "Bring us our morning meal. Indeed we have met with fatigue from this journey of ours"﴾ the ghadaa' (morning meal) is what is eaten at the beginning of the day; ﴿fatigue﴾ meaning weariness, and its reaching them was after they had passed beyond the place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 63:

﴿He said: Did you see?﴾ That is, pay attention, ﴿when we took refuge at the rock﴾ at that place, ﴿for I forgot the fish, and none but Satan made me forget it, so that I should mention it﴾. It is substituted for the pronoun (in "made me forget it"), a substitution of part (badal ishtimal), meaning: Satan made me forget its remembrance. ﴿And it took its way into the sea, wondrously﴾: "wondrously" is a second object (maf'ul thani), meaning that Musa and his servant marvelled at it, because of what had preceded in its explanation.

Musa said: "That" — i.e., the losing of the fish — "is what we were seeking," meaning we were seeking it, for it was a sign for us of the presence of the one we were seeking. "So they both turned back" — they returned "retracing their footsteps," following their own tracks back along the way, "and they came to the rock."

﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants﴾. He is al-Khidr (al-Khadir). ﴿We had given him mercy from Us﴾: prophethood (nubuwwa) according to one opinion, and sainthood (wilaya) according to another. Most scholars hold this latter view. ﴿And We had taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾: from Our side. ﴿Knowledge﴾ is the second object (maf'ul thani), meaning knowledge of the unseen. Al-Bukhari narrated the hadith: "Musa stood up to deliver a sermon among the Children of Israel, and he was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I. So Allah rebuked him, because he had not referred knowledge to Him. Allah revealed to him: Indeed I have a servant at the meeting place of the two seas, who is more knowledgeable than you. Musa said: O Lord, how can I reach him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket; wherever you lose the fish, he is there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then set off, and his servant Yusha' ibn Nun set off with him, until they came to the rock, and they put down their heads and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out of it, and fell into the sea. ﴿And it took its way into the sea, a tunnel﴾. Allah held back the flow of water from the fish, so it became like an arch over it. When he awoke, his companion forgot to tell him about the fish, so they continued the rest of their day and night, until in the morning Musa said to his servant: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾, up to His saying ﴿and it took its way into the sea, a marvel﴾. He said: the fish had a tunnel, and for Musa and his servant it was a marvel, etc."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 66:

﴿Musa said to him, "May I follow you on the condition that you teach me from what you have been taught, [some] right guidance?"﴾ That is, correct knowledge by which I may be guided. In another reading, the ra' is pronounced with a dammah and the shin is sukun (rushdan, pronounced ruzdan... ). He asked this because increase in knowledge is sought.

﴿And how can you be patient about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ In the preceding hadith, following this verse, [it is reported]: "O Musa, I have a knowledge from Allah that He taught me, which you do not know, and you have a knowledge from Allah that Allah taught you, which I do not know." His words, *khubran* (a verbal noun, *masdar*, meaning "in the sense of"), are equivalent to *lam tuhit* (you did not encompass), i.e., *lam tukhbar haqiqatahu* (you were not informed of its reality).

﴿He said: "You will find me, if God wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ That is, and not disobeying [any] command of yours, ﴿"in any matter."﴾ He qualified it with "if God wills" because he was not confident in himself regarding what he had committed to; and this is the custom of the prophets and the friends of God (awliya'), that they do not trust in themselves even for the blink of an eye.

He said, "If you follow me, then do not question me about anything" (﴿قالَ فَإنْ اتَّبَعْتنِي فَلا تَسْأَلنِي﴾). In another recitation (qirāʾa), the lām is read with a fatḥa and the nūn with a shadda, "فَلَا تَسَّأَلَنَّ" (fa-lā tassaʾalanna). The verse continues: "about anything" (﴿عَنْ شَيْء﴾) that you find objectionable from me "in your knowledge" (﴿تُنْكِرهُ مِنِّي فِي عِلْمك﴾), "and be patient" (﴿واصْبِرْ﴾) "until I make mention of it to you" (﴿حَتّى أُحْدِث لَك مِنهُ ذِكْرًا﴾), i.e., I will mention it to you along with its reason (ʿilla). So Mūsā accepted his condition, out of regard for the etiquette (adab) of the student toward the scholar.

﴿So they set out⦆ walking along the seashore. ﴿Until, when they boarded the ship⦆ which passed by them, ﴿he [al-Khidr] damaged it⦆ by prying loose one or two planks from its side toward the sea with an axe, when it had reached the deep waters. ﴿[Musa] said⦆ to him, ﴿"Have you damaged it in order to drown its people?⦆ In another reading, the first letter is read with a fatha (yā' with fatha) and the rā' with fatha, and "ahluhā" (its people) is read in the nominative (raf'), so that it reads "yaghraqa ahluhā" (its people drown). ﴿"Indeed you have done a terrible thing⦆" i.e., a great and objectionable deed. It is narrated that the water did not enter it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 73:

﴿He said: Do not blame me for what I forgot﴾, i.e., I was negligent in submitting to you and in abandoning objection against you. ﴿And do not burden me﴾, i.e., do not impose upon me ﴿difficulty in my affair﴾, i.e., hardship in my companionship with you; that is, deal with me in it with pardon and ease.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 74:

﴿So they set off﴾ after their departure from the ship, walking. ﴿Until, when they met a boy﴾ who had not reached puberty (al-hinth), playing with the children, the most handsome of them in face. ﴿So he killed him﴾ — al-Khadir killed him by slaughtering him with a knife while he lay on his side, or by pulling his head off with his hand, or by striking his head against the wall; these are the opinions. He used the conjunctive fa' here because the killing came immediately after the meeting. The answer to "idha" is what follows. If the instrument with which al-Khadir killed the boy is mentioned, or the description of the manner of his killing, there is no explicit text about it, and therefore the opinions on it have multiplied. These matters are of no importance, because what matters is that the killing actually took place. ﴿He [Musa] said﴾ to him: ﴿Have you killed a soul innocent﴾, meaning pure, one who had not reached the limit of legal responsibility. In another reading it is "zakiyyah" with the yaa' doubled and without an alif. ﴿Without a soul﴾, meaning he had not killed anyone. ﴿Indeed, you have done a thing monstrous﴾ — with the kaaf pronounced sukun and with damma — meaning a denounced (munkaran) thing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 75:

﴿He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ He added to what he had said before, "for there is no excuse here" (lia'dam al-'udhr huna).

Therefore ﴿He said: If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as your companion﴾, i.e., after this time, ﴿do not keep me as your companion﴾, do not leave me, I would follow you; ﴿you have already received an excuse from me﴾, with the two readings of shaddah and its lightening (takhfif), from my side, ﴿an excuse﴾ for parting from you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 77:

﴿So they set off, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. And they found in it a wall⁠—﴾ It was Antioch. ﴿They asked its people for food﴾ seeking food from them as hospitality. ﴿But they refused to host them. And they found in it a wall﴾ its height being a hundred cubits. ﴿About to collapse﴾ meaning, about to fall down, because of its leaning. ﴿So he set it upright﴾ al-Khidr, with his hand. ﴿Said﴾ to him Musa, ﴿"If you had wished, you could have taken for it a wage"﴾ — and in another reading, "لَتَخِذْت" (latakhadhta) — ﴿"a payment"﴾ a fee, since they did not host us, although we were in need of food.

﴿He said﴾ to him, al-Khiḍr: ﴿This is parting﴾, i.e., the time of parting, ﴿between me and you﴾. Here the Arabic word بَيْن (bayn, "between") is put in annexation (idafa, a construction in which one noun is linked to the noun that follows it) to a noun that is not plural. This is permitted because it is repeated with the conjunction "and" (wa), so the construction is "between me and you." ﴿I will inform you﴾ of the meaning of what you did not have patience for, before my parting from you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 79:

﴿As for the ship, it belonged to poor people﴾ — ten of them — ﴿who worked on the sea﴾, with it, hiring it out for earnings, seeking gain. ﴿So I wished to damage it, for behind them﴾ — when they returned — or ahead of them, now — ﴿was a king﴾, an unbeliever, ﴿who seized every ship﴾ that was sound ﴿by force﴾. Its being in the accusative (naṣb) is as an absolute object (maṣdar) clarifying the type of seizing.

And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and We feared that he would overburden them with rebellion and disbelief. For, as in the hadith narrated by Muslim, he was created as a disbeliever. Had he lived, that would have burdened them, because of their love for him, so that they would follow him in that.

Qur'anic quotations: "So We intended that their Lord should replace them with one better than him in purity" — the passage's quotation is ﴿فَأَرَدْنا أنْ يُبَدِّلهُما﴾ ... ﴿رَبّهما خَيْرًا مِنهُ زَكاة﴾ ... ﴿وأَقْرَب﴾ ... ﴿رُحْمًا﴾.

Translation:

﴿So We intended that He would replace them﴾ (read with both the doubled and the single-letter forms of the verb), ﴿with their Lord giving them one better than him in purity﴾, i.e., righteousness and piety, ﴿and nearer in mercy﴾ from him, ﴿in mercy﴾ (read with both the vowelled and unvowelled forms of the ḥāʾ), meaning compassion, which is dutifulness toward his two parents. So God replaced them with a girl who married a prophet, and she bore a prophet, through whom God guided a community.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 82:

﴿And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them⁠﴾ — a buried property of gold and silver, ﴿and their father had been righteous﴾, so they were protected by his righteousness in their persons and their wealth. ﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity⁠﴾ — i.e., attain the soundness of their judgment, ﴿and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord⁠﴾ — a purpose clause (maf'ul lahu) whose governing verb is "intended" (arada). ﴿And I did it not of my own accord⁠﴾ — i.e., what was mentioned of tearing the ship, killing the boy, and rebuilding the wall was not by my own choice, but by a command of inspiration from God. ﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience⁠﴾. It is said "ista'ala" and "istata'a" both mean "to be able" (atāqa); so in this and the preceding verse there is a combination of the two dialects, and the expression was varied in: "fa-aradtu," "fa-aradna," "fa-arada rabbuka."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 83:

﴿And they ask you﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿about Dhu'l-Qarnayn﴾. His name was Alexander (al-Iskandar), and he was not a prophet. ﴿Say: I will recite﴾, i.e., I will relate ﴿to you of him﴾, of his condition, ﴿a report﴾, i.e., news.
Indeed, We established him in the land by making travel through it easy for him, and We gave him from every thing he needed a means (sabab), a way that brings him to his purpose.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 85:

﴿Then he followed a way﴾ He took a path towards the west.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 86:

﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun﴾, the place of its setting, ﴿he found it setting in a muddy spring﴾, containing mud (ḥama'a), which is black clay; and its setting in the spring was in the view of the eye (fī ra'y al-ʿayn), but otherwise it is far greater than the world. ﴿And he found beside it﴾, i.e., beside the spring, ﴿a people﴾ who were disbelievers. ﴿We said: O Dhu'l-Qarnayn﴾, by inspiration, ﴿either you punish﴾ the people by killing, ﴿or you adopt among them goodness﴾ by taking them captive.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 87:

﴿He said: "As for him who does wrong"﴾ by associating partners with God, ﴿"we will punish him"﴾ by killing him, ﴿"then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment"﴾ with the k being either sukun or damma, meaning severe, in the Fire.

﴿As for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, he will have the reward of the best﴾, i.e., Paradise. The genitive construction (al-idafa) here is for explanation (li-l-bayan). In another recitation, *jaza'* is read in the accusative with tanwin, *jaza'an*. Al-Farra' said: its accusative is by way of specification (al-tafsir), i.e., to indicate the respect in which (li-jihat al-nisba) the reward applies. ﴿And We shall tell him, from Our command, ease﴾, i.e., We shall command him with what is easy for him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 18, verse 89:

﴿Then he followed a way﴾ toward the east.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 90:

﴿Until, when he reached the rising-place of the sun﴾, the place where it rises, ﴿he found it rising over a people﴾, they were the Zanj (Zanj: the Black peoples of East Africa), ﴿for whom We had made no shelter from it﴾, i.e., from the sun, ﴿no cover﴾, of clothing or roof, because their land does not bear buildings, and they have burrows in which they hide when the sun rises and emerge when it has risen high.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 91:

﴿Thus it was﴾ i.e., the matter is as We have said, ﴿and We encompassed what was with him﴾ i.e., with Dhu'l-Qarnayn of the equipment, the soldiers and other things, ﴿in knowledge﴾ i.e., knowledge.

"Until, when he reached between the two barriers," with the sin read with a fatha and also with a damma here. Between them were two mountains at the far end of the lands of the Turks, and the Barrier of Alexander (Sadd al-Iskandar) was between them, as will come later. "He found beside them" means in front of them, "a people who could hardly understand speech" means they did not understand it except after great slowness. In one qira'a (variant recitation), the verb is read as يُفْقِهُونَ, with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the qaf.

They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Yajuj and Majuj ﴿are corrupting in the earth﴾." The name is pronounced with the hamza and without it (يأجوج ومأجوج, *Yājūj wa-Mājūj*, with or without the hamza). Both are non-Arabic names for two tribes, which is why they are not declined (*lam yanṣarifā*, that is, treated as diptotes). They corrupt the earth through plundering and oppression when they come out against us.

﴿So shall we assign for you a tribute (خرجا, *kharjan*)?﴾ That is, a sum of wealth. In another reading it is read as خراجا (*kharājan*).

﴿On condition that you place between us and them a barrier (سدا, *saddan*)﴾, a partition that prevents them from reaching us.

"He said: 'That in which my Lord has established me is better' — (in another reading, with two nuns and without assimilation) — 'than your tribute. So help me with strength, and I will make between you and them a barrier.'"

Let me give the full translation with the glosses as the passage requires:

﴿He said: "What my Lord has established me in is better"﴾ (in another reading, the two nuns are pronounced separately, without idgham, i.e. assimilation) ﴿—of wealth and other things—"is better"﴾ than your tribute, which you propose to give me, so I have no need of it. ﴿"But I will build for you a barrier as a voluntary act of charity. So help me with strength"﴾ for what I require of you, ﴿"between you and them, a barrier"﴾, a strong, fortified barrier.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 96:

﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾, pieces proportioned to the stones with which it is built, and he placed between them the firewood and coal. ﴿Until, when he had leveled [the gap] between the two cliffs﴾, [the word ṣadafayn is read with both letters dammed and fatḥa, or with the first dammed and the second sakin]; i.e., the two sides of the mountains, by building and placing the bellows and fire around that. ﴿He said: Blow﴾, so they blew, ﴿until, when he had made it﴾, i.e., the iron, ﴿fire﴾, i.e., like fire, ﴿he said: Bring me molten copper to pour over it﴾, [qiṭr is] the melted copper. The two verbs contend over it (tanāzaʿa fīhi al-fiʿlān), and the first is omitted because the second is made to govern it. [The meaning is:] molten copper poured over the heated iron, so it entered between its blocks and they became one single thing.
﴿So they were not able﴾ i.e., Gog and Magog, ﴿to scale it﴾ (to climb over its top), because of its height and smoothness, ﴿nor could they make a breach in it﴾ because of its hardness and thickness.

Dhul-Qarnayn said: "This" (i.e., the barrier, or the ability to build it) "is a mercy from my Lord," a blessing, "for it is a barrier against their coming out." "So when the promise of my Lord comes," i.e., the emergence of Gog and Magog, which is near the Resurrection, "He will make it level, flattened," crushed and spread out. "And the promise of my Lord is ever true," i.e., their emergence and other things are certainly going to happen.

﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging against one another﴾, the day of their coming out, [surging] into one another, mingling with each other because of their great number. ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾, meaning the trumpet (al-qarn), for the Resurrection. ﴿Then We will gather them﴾, meaning the creation, into one place on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 100:

﴿And We presented﴾ We brought near

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 101:

﴿Those whose eyes were in a veil from My remembrance﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the disbelievers"; that is, from the Qur'an, so they are blind and do not gain guidance through it. ﴿And they were unable to hear﴾ means they were not able to listen to what the Prophet recited to them, out of hatred for him, so they do not believe in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 102:

﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me?﴾ That is, My angels, and Jesus and Ezra (ʿUzayr). ﴿As protectors besides Me﴾ — i.e., as lords. "Protectors" (awliyāʾ) is the second object of "yattakhidhū" (take). The second object of "ḥasiba" (think) is omitted; its meaning is: "Do they suppose that the taking mentioned will not anger Me, and that I will not punish them for it? No indeed!" ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers﴾ — these and others — ﴿as a welcome (nuzul)﴾, i.e., it is prepared for them like a dwelling prepared for a guest.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 103:

﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who lose the most in their deeds?﴾ "Al-akhsarin a'mala" is a tamyiz (specification), which agrees with the thing specified (al-mumayyaz) and clarifies it by His saying:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 104:

﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world⦆ their deeds became void. ﴿While they think⦆ they suppose ﴿that they are doing good work⦆ deeds for which they will be rewarded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 105:

﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾ by the proofs of His oneness from the Qur'an and other than it, ﴿and in meeting Him﴾, i.e., and in the resurrection, the reckoning, the reward and the punishment, ﴿so their deeds have become worthless﴾, i.e., became void, ﴿and We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾, i.e., We will not give them any value.

This is the Tafsir al-Jalalayn commentary on Surah 18 (al-Kahf), verse 106.

﴿That﴾ i.e., the matter I have mentioned concerning the nullification of their deeds and other things, is the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿their recompense is Hellfire, because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in mockery﴾, i.e., mocked at them both.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 107:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — for them were﴾ in the knowledge of Allah ﴿the Gardens of Firdaws﴾ it is the middle of Paradise and its highest part, and the genitive construction with it is for specification ﴿as a lodging﴾ a dwelling place

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 108:

﴿Abiding therein forever, they will not desire any removal from it.﴾ (yabghūna: they seek) ﴿from it any removal﴾ (ḥiwalan: a transfer, a moving) to something other than it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 109:

﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord,﴾ that is, its water, ﴿ink (midad)﴾ being that with which one writes, ﴿the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted,﴾ which indicate His wisdom and wonders, if they were written with it, ﴿the sea would be exhausted in writing them,﴾ ﴿before the words of my Lord are exhausted,﴾ with the ta' and the ya' (as two readings): they would come to an end. ﴿And even if We brought the like of it,﴾ that is, the sea, ﴿as a supplement (madadan)﴾ added to it, ﴿it would be exhausted, and they [the words] would not come to an end.﴾ Its being accusative is as a specification (tamyiz).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 18, verse 110:

﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is but one God."﴾ [A human being (ādamī) like you.] ["That" (anna) in "annamā" is the one softened (al-mukaffafa) by "mā" and remains in its verbal (maṣdariyya) function. The meaning is: it is revealed to me the oneness (waḥdāniyya) of God.] ﴿So whoever hopes (yarjū), i.e., expects (yāmul), to meet his Lord, through resurrection (al-baʿth) and recompense (al-jazāʾ),﴾ ﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord,﴾ i.e., in it, by showing off (an yurāʾiya).
